To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the behavioural characteristics of Argentinean managers perceived as effective are similar to those of managers perceived as effective in other cultures.

Argentinean managers who are effective are perceived by employees as supportive, considerate and fair, and that Argentinean managers are perceived by employees to be ineffective when they are autocratic, uncommunicative, and uninvolved in the work of their employees.
effective managers are those who are supportive, caring, motivating, fair minded, participative, and who act in an open, approachable manner.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the behavioural dimensions of managerial effectiveness.

the behavioural determinants of effective managers in a Latin American context, and it contributes to the existing literature by offering an alternative perspective on managerial effectiveness, which is based on the perceptions of employees rather than those of the manager's superiors.
the behavioural determinants of perceived effectiveness, rather than effectiveness itself.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Argentinean managers and employees interviewed in this study, in the context of this research project, perceived the following as the most important behaviours that distinguished between effective and ineffective managerial behaviour: (1) supportive, considerate behaviour (2) motivating behaviour (3) fair minded behaviour (4) good decision maker (5) communicative behaviour (6) participative behaviour (7) approachable behaviour (8) actively involved behaviour (9) caring behaviour (10) role model behaviour.
Argentinean employees perceive as effective those leaders who behave in a manner consistent with the values and beliefs of the Argentinian culture.
Argentineans perceive managers as effective when they behave in a democratic and participative manner.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Argentineans prefer managers who are supportive of their employees and are actively involved in their work.
Argentineans prefer managers who are supportive and considerate, and who actively involve subordinates in the decision making process.
the Argentinean managers and employees are not that different from managers and employees from other cultures.
The main takeaway from our work is that
effective managers are not necessarily those with a high level of power and authority, but rather those with the ability to inspire and influence others to achieve organizational objectives.
effective managerial behaviours are context specific, and that they are influenced by the culture and context of the organization.
Argentinean managers and their subordinates perceive effective leadership as a combination of democratic, participative and supportive behaviours.
